subject: general
question: Godaan is a novel written by Munshi Premchand, published in the year _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1936.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Godaan is a **Hindi novel **written by **Munshi Premchand**, published in the year **1936.**
 
• It was first published in 1936 and is considered one of** Premchand's most renowned works.**
 
• Munshi Premchand, whose real name was** Dhanpat Rai Srivastava,** was** born on July 31, 1880, in Lamhi, near Varanasi.**
 
• His literary contributions earned him the title of** "Upanyas Samrat"** (Emperor of Novels).
 
• Some of his famous novels are** Nirmala, Rangbhoomi, Gaban, Kafan etc.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rangbhoomi**

 
 
• It was published in **1924** and is considered one of Munshi Premchand's significant works.
 
• This novel explores various social issues prevalent in Indian society during the **colonial era, such as corruption, exploitation, and the struggle for justice.**
 
• It revolves around the world of theatre, highlighting the challenges and complexities faced by artists, their conflicts, and their efforts to bring about social change through their art.
 
 
 
• **Gaban**
 
 
• It was published in **1931** and is considered one of Munshi Premchand's notable works.
 
• The novel delves into **themes of greed, social hypocrisy, and the consequences of materialism in Indian society.**
 
• The story revolves around Ramanath, the main character, who succumbs to his desires for wealth and social status. The novel follows his journey as he becomes entangled in a web of deceit and faces the consequences of his actions.
 
 
 
• **Kafan**
 
 
• It depicts the bleak and tragic life of a poor peasant named Gheesu and his son Madhav, who struggle with extreme poverty and societal indifference.
 
• The story explores **themes of poverty, social inequality, and the dehumanizing effects of a rigid caste system **prevalent in rural Indian society.
 
• "Kafan" serves as a sharp critique of the oppressive social conditions and the apathy of the privileged classes towards the** suffering of the poor.**
